cases.name: the keeper's thread, from the noticeboard to the lit lamp, seen from the quay

told: WELCOME TO PORTHLEVEN. Type help for the commands you can use, look to see where you are, and a direction such as north to walk. Tide times are in the crate. THE SHIP is open, Jory presiding. LAMP UNLIT: the lighthouse has been dark since the storm, and its keeper, Ezra Trethewey, has not been seen. Anyone with news, see the harbourmaster.

The Square
A cobbled square around a granite cross. The Ship stands on the west side and a chandler's shop on the east; a lane climbs north out of town, and the harbour lies south.

You see: the cross
Exits: north, east, west, south

Chandler's Shop
Rope, tar, brass fittings and oilskins crowd every shelf. Nobody minds the shop, but there's an honesty box on the counter.

You see: the matches, the rope
There is: the honesty box
Exits: west
Taken.

The Ship
A low-beamed bar, its ceiling hung with glass floats and an old ship's wheel. A fire smokes in the grate, and a door at the back leads north.

There is: the counter
Also here: Jory
Exits: north, east

ada: Jory says, "Welcome aboard The Ship, ada."

told: Jory slides the tankard out of your reach. "That's paid for, that is."

Back Room
A cramped room stacked with barrels. Coats nobody came back for hang on a row of pegs.

There is: the lost property box
Exits: south
Opening the lost property box reveals: the oilskin, the torn page.
Taken.

14th. Wind backing south-west, glass falling fast. Lamp trimmed and lit at dusk. The spare key to the lamp room is in the shed at the cottage, as ever. If the weather holds I shall... The rest is torn away.

ada: Jory says, "That torn page? Washed up on the slipway after the storm. It's in the lost property box in the back."

Short turf and sea pinks run out to a rocky point. East, a causeway of weed-slick stones crosses to the lighthouse on its island.

Lighthouse
The whitewashed foot of the lighthouse tower. Coils of rope and a can of paraffin stand by an iron stair that winds up into the dark.

Exits: up (closed), west
The iron door is closed.

(with the brass key)

Opened.

Lamp Room
A round room of glass at the top of the tower, the great lamp at its centre. Through the salt-crusted panes you can see the whole harbour.

You see: the lamp, the logbook
Exits: down

The keeper's last entry, after the torn page: 15th. Storm through the night. A light seen out past the Bar, where no light should be. Took the punt out at first ebb to look. Mrs Pascoe will say I'm a fool. Nothing is written after it.
You strike a storm match and hold it to the wick. The lamp catches, the great lens begins to turn, and its beam swings out across the sea.

bob: Out on its island, the lighthouse flares into life, and its beam sweeps across the harbour.

told: The lamp is already lit.

Harbour Steps
Worn granite steps climb from the ferry landing to the quay. Gulls squabble on the bollards, and the town rises behind you in terraces of slate and whitewash.

You see: the sea, the noticeboard
There is: the crate
Also here: Morwenna
Exits: north, south, east, west

The tide is out. Boats lean on their keels in the harbour mud, and past the headland the causeway to the lighthouse stands clear of the water. The lighthouse beam sweeps across the harbour.

The tide is out. Boats lean on their keels in the harbour mud, and past the headland the causeway to the lighthouse stands clear of the water.
You say, "how is the tide?"

ada: Morwenna says, "It's out now, but it turns quick here. Don't get caught on the far side."
The tide turns, and the sea comes creeping back across the mud.
Morwenna says, "Tide's turned. The causeway will be under in no time."

told: You say, "and now, the tide?"

ada: Morwenna says, "The tide's in. Nobody crosses to the lighthouse till it ebbs."

told: The tide is in, and the harbour is full of grey-green water.
